newsitem.title: GERMANY: UK's Clarke says G7 reached agreement on dollar.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke says G7 reached agreement on dollar.

text.p: Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Saturday that the seven most industrialised nations, conducting a one-day economic policy meeting in Berlin, reached an agreement on the dollar.

Asked by reporters whether the meeting had been productive Clarke said:"Yes, it has been productive." Asked also whether an agreement had been reached on the dollar, Clarke answered: "There has been an agreement and we will make an announcement in due course."

Members of the G7 -- the U.S. Germany, Japan, France, Italy, Canada and Britain -- were in Berlin for one day meetings to discuss, among other things, the levels of the dollar and Europe's progress towards monetary union.
Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said he was satisfied with the current dollar level but that the correction process ought to end very soon.

U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin on Friday signalled a subtle shift in U.S. policy when he said that the U.S. had been interested in a strong dollar but that this had been the case for some time now.
Individual nations plans to hold news briefings later this afternoon.
